11867|3f5ede7c.name: Woo Ping
11867|3f5ede7c.text: Have you come seeking training in the ways of armed combat?

1289|ed056522.name: Gunther Weller
1289|ed056522.text: Best deals in all of Stormwind my friend, won't find any better. Now, what can I help you with?

1289|fe52f4ea.name: Gunther Weller
1289|fe52f4ea.text: Just browsing my wares or is there something specific I can help you find today?

1309|0624ab70.name: Wynne Larson
1309|0624ab70.text: Since the fall of Dalaran and the destruction of Quel'Thalas, wares of this sort have been hard to come by. But Lucan Cordell and some of our other Tradesman have been doing a fine job of filling our orders with quality merchandise.

1310|23d8b931.name: Evan Larson
1310|23d8b931.text: I sell only the finest arcane gear, made by the crafters and mages here in the city of Stormwind.

1347|23d8b931.name: Alexandra Bolero
1347|23d8b931.text: I sell only the finest arcane gear, made by the crafters and mages here in the city of Stormwind.

1573|10cfc531.name: Gryth Thurden
1573|10cfc531.text: The Wildhammer dwarves might have fast steeds, but can those Aerie Peak gryphons stand the heat of The Great Forge?  I think not!

2409|c5ceacbe.name: Felicia Maline
2409|c5ceacbe.text: Where would you like to fly to?

2457|105cd232.name: John Burnside
2457|105cd232.text: No one's ever stolen anything out of here. Not in the whole history of... the whole history!

352|c23f1156.name: Dungar Longdrink
352|c23f1156.text: These great beasts know paths that ye can't find on foot, they'll get ye there fast and maybe show ye something new at the same time.

3838|43c9021b.name: Vesprystus
3838|43c9021b.text: To maintain our link to the mainland, we have hippogryphs constantly flying between Rut'theran Village and Darkshore.

3841|ab4871bb.name: Caylais Moonfeather
3841|ab4871bb.text: The Hippogryph is a noble beast, proud and swift.  They are an honor to train, and can quickly take their rider a great distance.

4200|c2e88775.name: Laird
4200|c2e88775.text: Although the coast of Darkshore is more dangerous than that of Teldrassil, many fishers find profit here.

5564|568f7020.name: Simon Tanner
5564|568f7020.text: Hmm, I guess I can take on another student. Well, don't just stand there. Tell me what you're looking to learn.

5565|877c4b1d.name: Jillian Tanner
5565|877c4b1d.text: I sell only the best gear, tested and true. And the prices are set, so if you want to haggle then go find a Goblin.

928|837f02f9.name: Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker
928|837f02f9.text: May the Light protect you this day.

101-complete.name: Madame Eva
101-complete.text: Very wise of you, $N.  This Totem of Infliction will help to protect you against the evil which lurks throughout Azeroth and beyond.  When you feel threatened, hold this totem and take comfort in its magical aura.  Be brave, fair $c.  You will need all the courage you can muster for I see much bloodshed in your future.
101-complete.title: The Totem of Infliction

101-progress.name: Madame Eva
101-progress.text: Bring to me 10 ghoul fangs, 10 skeleton fingers and 5 vials of spider venom.  For you I shall enchant a Totem of Infliction which will harm those who attempt violent acts against you.
101-progress.title: The Totem of Infliction

1275-accept.name: Gershala Nightwhisper
1275-accept.text:
Foolish blood elves toil with demonic magic. Have they not witnessed what happened with the naga and with the satyrs of Kalimdor?

I fear that the blood elves will meet a similar deformation. Azeroth cannot afford to give birth to another vile race of monsters.

I wish to study the brain stems of the satyr and naga so that I might deduce what fate the elves are headed toward. In Blackfathom Deeps, on the coast of Ashenvale, you will find both satyr and naga.

'Tis a long journey, $N.
1275-accept.title: Researching the Corruption

149-complete.name: Blind Mary
149-complete.text:
What is this?  A comb?  It's lovely!  And it glides through my hair as if it weren't the stiff, stringy horror that it is.

Oh, if only I had a mirror...
149-complete.title: Ghost Hair Thread

149-progress.name: Blind Mary
149-progress.text:
<Sob> Oh please, don't look at me!  I tore out these eyes with my own hands, but I can still feel your gaze!

I'm hideous!  Hideous!  Please, look away!!
149-progress.title: Ghost Hair Thread

154-accept.name: Blind Mary
154-accept.text:
NO!!!!!

Take it, take this comb away from me!

I'm a monster, and no one will ever think me lovely again!
154-accept.title: Return the Comb

154-complete.name: Madame Eva
154-complete.text: I can make a spool of Ghost Hair Thread with this, and have a few strands to spare.  Here are some coins for those extra strands.
154-complete.title: Return the Comb

154-progress.name: Madame Eva
154-progress.text: I sense that you have seen Blind Mary.  You have my Comb...?
154-progress.title: Return the Comb

156-accept.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
156-accept.text:
If you bring me some rot blossoms then I can brew you up a batch of zombie juice.

Rot blossoms grow in strange places.  In particular, I hear you can find them inside the skulls of Skeletal Horrors and Skeletal Fiends... not that I've gotten close enough to look!

The Raven Hill Cemetery and the Tranquil Gardens are both lousy with those skeletons.  You may as well get rid of them while you're looking for rot blossoms.  The town of Darkshire would be grateful.
156-accept.title: Gather Rot Blossoms

156-complete.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
156-complete.text:
Good,  you got the rot blossoms.  And I'll tell Althea Ebonlocke of the Night Watch that you were killing skeletons.

Keeping the people of Darkshire safe is a grim burden for the Night Watch, and news that others are helping stem the tide of fiends in Duskwood is welcome news indeed.
156-complete.title: Gather Rot Blossoms

156-progress.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
156-progress.text: Hi, $N.  Do you have those rot blossoms for me yet?
156-progress.title: Gather Rot Blossoms

157-accept.name: Madame Eva
157-accept.text: Here is your thread, $N.  It has a thousand uses, from binding evil spirits to sewing life into inanimate objects.
157-accept.title: Deliver the Thread

157-complete.name: Abercrombie
157-complete.text:
Delightful!  This will do splendidly...

Here, good $N, take this as payment for your honorable deed.
157-complete.title: Deliver the Thread

157-progress.name: Abercrombie
157-progress.text: I need to string the Ghost Hair Thread along my door and my windows to keep out unwanted spirits.  Did you get it for me?
157-progress.title: Deliver the Thread

158-accept.name: Abercrombie
158-accept.text:
I need a bottle of a certain liquor - Zombie Juice.  Tavernkeep Smitts at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire should have some.

And please hurry, $N.  These nights get cold, and I need that drink to put fire in my veins again!
158-accept.title: Zombie Juice

158-complete.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
158-complete.text: You need some Zombie Juice, do you?  Hmm...that's some strong stuff - I don't usually get requests for it.
158-complete.title: Zombie Juice

159-accept.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
159-accept.text:
Here's your Zombie Juice...

...and be careful with this stuff.  It's strong enough to raise the dead!
159-accept.title: Juice Delivery

173-accept.name: Calor
173-accept.text:
Darkness seems drawn inexorably to Duskwood. Master Carevin's quest is the expulsion of evil and heresy. Through our efforts are the people of Darkshire kept safe.

You believe yourself worthy to join us?

I once thought as you. Disillusioned by the complacency of the Watch, I joined Master Carevin. If you wish to prove yourself, it will not be through words.

Test your skills against the Nightbane Shadow Weaver worgen in Brightwood Grove--bright, hah!--and the Rotting Orchard.
173-accept.title: Worgen in the Woods

174-accept.name: Viktori Prism'Antras
174-accept.text:
My Gnomish friend, Cog, has promised to help me build a device which will let me peer towards the stars.  A truth exists, beyond magic, that can explain the strange transformation in the forest.

Bring to me a bronze tube made by a skilled engineer.  That is the first step, according to Cog's blueprint.
174-accept.title: Look to the Stars

174-complete.name: Viktori Prism'Antras
174-complete.text: This is perfect, $N.  The first step is complete!
174-complete.title: Look to the Stars

174-progress.name: Viktori Prism'Antras
174-progress.text: Have you found a skilled engineer to create a bronze tube yet?
174-progress.title: Look to the Stars

175-accept.name: Viktori Prism'Antras
175-accept.text: According to Cog's blueprint, what I need now is a way to reflect light.  I remember a woman by the name of Mary who became well known around these parts for always carrying a looking glass.  Perhaps you can track Mary down and see if she might lend us a reflective surface for this project?  I believe she once resided in southern Duskwood. . .
175-accept.title: Look to the Stars

175-complete.name: Blind Mary
175-complete.text: Why yes, I used to own a looking glass.
175-complete.title: Look to the Stars

177-accept.name: Blind Mary
177-accept.text: The looking glass was one of my finest treasures until. . .the incident.  After that happened, I discarded it behind the barn.  There was an Insane Ghoul who used to roam back there.  Perhaps he picked it up.  Rumor has it the devilish beast resides in the Tranquil Gardens Cemetery.
177-accept.title: Look to the Stars

177-complete.name: Viktori Prism'Antras
177-complete.text: Most superb!  This will work perfectly.  Many thanks!
177-complete.title: Look to the Stars

177-progress.name: Viktori Prism'Antras
177-progress.text: I showed Cog the beginnings of our star-viewing machine.  He was impressed.  Did you happen to find a reflective device?
177-progress.title: Look to the Stars

181-accept.name: Viktori Prism'Antras
181-accept.text:
Now there is just one more item needed to complete this device.  Cog's blueprint calls for a lens of some sort.  The only lens I know of that would be large enough will be very difficult to acquire.

There is an ogre by the name of Zzarc'Vul who resides in the mound in southern Duskwood.  If you can, bring to me his monocle and I will use that as our lens!
181-accept.title: Look to the Stars

230-accept.name: Unknown
230-accept.text:
Digging through the mound, you find a small, dirt-stained book.

The book has no title, but...it has information Sven would like to know.
230-accept.title: Sven's Camp

230-complete.name: Sven Yorgen
230-complete.text:
<Sven reads the book's pages, then slams it shut.>

That shadowy figure I saw was a witness to my family's death!  There are questions I'd like to ask that man...if only I knew who he was!
230-complete.title: Sven's Camp

230-progress.name: Sven Yorgen
230-progress.text: You found what??  Please, let me see it...
230-progress.title: Sven's Camp

245-accept.name: Watcher Dodds
245-accept.text:
Hail, $c. Perhaps you've seen those spiders that have taken over the western border? The eight-legged menaces are too much for us to handle, and the Commander hasn't enough manpower to spare so far from Darkshire.

I hate to ask this of you, but you seem like you might be able to handle them. I can't promise you anything of great value, but I can reward you if you can help root out the filthy bugs.

Oh, and a word of advice, you'll want to avoid their venom if you can.
245-accept.title: Eight-Legged Menaces

245-complete.name: Watcher Dodds
245-complete.text: Ah! You're back. And not too much worse for wear, it'd seem. Of course, $N, the Night Watch is grateful for your work, and I did promise you a reward, so here.
245-complete.title: Eight-Legged Menaces

248-accept.name: Unknown
248-accept.text:
I have been watching the Tower of Ilgalar, and can detect that Morganth is in conflict with the Orcs in Stonewatch Keep.  I do not know the reason behind their contention, but you may aid me in unraveling this mystery.

Take another Glyph of Azora, then go to the top of the intact watch tower beside Stonewatch Keep.

Find a suitable object on which to place the Glyph.  A chest or a jar -- some place where the glyph will not be noticed -- will suit my purpose.
248-accept.title: Looking Further

248-complete.name: Unknown
248-complete.text: It is a suitable vessel for the Glyph of Azora, allowing Theocritus to delve into the minds within Stonewatch Keep.
248-complete.title: Looking Further

248-progress.name: Unknown
248-progress.text: This jar once held a foul-smelling liquor, but now lies empty and forgotten on a pair of barrels.
248-progress.title: Looking Further

262-accept.name: Sven Yorgen
262-accept.text:
I must know who was that skulker in the shadows I saw the night my family was killed!

Please, $N, you have shown your resourcefulness.  Please find that shadowy figure.  I must learn what secrets he holds!

I do not have clues that you do not already know, but here - take the book you found at my farm.  Perhaps some of the townsfolk can link this book with its owner.
262-accept.title: The Shadowy Figure

262-complete.name: Madame Eva
262-complete.text:
Hmm... Someone handled this book recently, someone who is driven by revenge.  But the impressions left on it, at least the impressions from the original owner, are faint.

I can tell, however, that the original owner of this book is not a native of Darkshire.
262-complete.title: The Shadowy Figure

262-progress.name: Madame Eva
262-progress.text: If you have something that belongs to the shadowy figure for whom you seek, then let me see it.  I may be able to divine something of its owner.
262-progress.title: The Shadowy Figure

265-accept.name: Madame Eva
265-accept.text:
Here is your book back, $N, and I bid you fortune with your search.  If you ask others in town, perhaps they can offer you more clues.

And here is one more for you - although the author of this book is a stranger to Darkshire, the book itself was purchased here.
265-accept.title: The Shadowy Search Continues

265-complete.name: Clerk Daltry
265-complete.text:
Ah, yes.  I sold this book a month ago to a shady person.  He didn't tell me his name, but he was a nervous, jittery chap, always looking over his shoulder.

I hope that helps you...
265-complete.title: The Shadowy Search Continues

265-progress.name: Clerk Daltry
265-progress.text:
Sometimes I'll sell blank books to scholars and mages, or to anyone who wants to keep a journal.

I remember well everyone to whom I sold a book within the last few months...
265-progress.title: The Shadowy Search Continues

266-accept.name: Clerk Daltry
266-accept.text:
Here is your book, and good luck with your inquiries.

You might want to expand your search to the inn.  If the person whom you seek spent time in town, then chances are someone saw him there.
266-accept.title: Inquire at the Inn

266-complete.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
266-complete.text:
Oh yeah, I remember this book.  Its owner rented a room for a few days, and spent his nights at the bar, writing.

He left town in a hurry, muttering about being hunted by...something.  Last I saw him he was heading west out of town, looking for a new spot to hide.

The first place he'd find to the west is Raven Hill...
266-complete.title: Inquire at the Inn

266-progress.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
266-progress.text:
The Scarlet Raven doesn't see the business it used to, but we still do get travelers passing through.

If you can describe the person you're looking for, maybe I'll remember him.
266-progress.title: Inquire at the Inn

268-accept.name: Jitters
268-accept.text:
The book you found was only half finished.  I had to leave it at Sven's farm when I fled there...

Here.  Take my completed journal to Sven.  It describes more fully what happened at his farm.

Although this journal has been my only company these past weeks, if giving it up keeps me from having to face Sven and his wrath, then I do it willingly!
268-accept.title: Return to Sven

268-complete.name: Sven Yorgen
268-complete.text: This journal explains much to me, and sets me on the path against the dark riders!  I have seen these riders in Duskwood, and have seen them speak with the wizard Morbent Fel, at the Forlorn Rowe.
268-complete.title: Return to Sven

268-progress.name: Sven Yorgen
268-progress.text: Did you find who the Shadowy Figure was?
268-progress.title: Return to Sven

275-accept.name: Rethiel the Greenwarden
275-accept.text:
I do not know why, but a festering grows within the Wetlands. Fen Creepers have risen. They are diseased, fevered blisters on the land, and for the fever to break they must be dispatched and allowed to settle back into the marshes.

The Fen Creepers shamble amidst the waterways of the Wetlands.
275-accept.title: Blisters on the Land

277-complete.name: Rethiel the Greenwarden
277-complete.text: ... thank you. I will smash these flints and cast them into the sea, so that they may never again be used to burn living wood.
277-complete.title: Fire Taboo

277-progress.name: Rethiel the Greenwarden
277-progress.text: Do you have the Gnolls' tools for fire?
277-progress.title: Fire Taboo

281-complete.name: Unknown
281-complete.text:
This crate is covered with clawed scratches, and the marks of water damage.  Prying it open reveals soggy and rotted straw, as if something of value was stored in the crate.  You search through the straw...

...and find an armload of red-colored bottles.
281-complete.title: Reclaiming Goods

284-accept.name: Unknown
284-accept.text:
You thoroughly search this cluster of Murloc hovels, and find no trace of the Menethil Statuette.

Perhaps one of the two nearby hovels to the north and northeast will have more clues.
284-accept.title: The Search Continues

284-complete.name: Unknown
284-complete.text:
This barrel is largely untouched.  Prying it open...

...you are assaulted by the pungent odor of cheese.  It's a little wet, but still tasty!
284-complete.title: The Search Continues

285-accept.name: Unknown
285-accept.text:
This grouping of Murloc hovels, after a thorough inspection, reveals nothing.

...but you're certain that the next clue you find will be fruitful.

One of the hovels to the north must have the Menethil Statuette!
285-accept.title: Search More Hovels

285-complete.name: Unknown
285-complete.text: This barrel is halfway buried amidst the mud and grass ...
285-complete.title: Search More Hovels

286-accept.name: Unknown
286-accept.text:
After pulling the barrel free from the muck and opening it, a silvery figurine is found packed in fine straw.  It depicts a young, long-haired Paladin with hammer upraised.

This must be the Menethil Statuette!  You must now return it to Karl Boran in Menethil Harbor.
286-accept.title: Return the Statuette

286-complete.name: Karl Boran
286-complete.text:
The captain of the Blind Princess will be relieved to hear this precious cargo has been recovered.  You have well earned this payment for services rendered.

It is good to see dependable folk like you, especially in trying times such as these.
286-complete.title: Return the Statuette

294-complete.name: Ormer Ironbraid
294-complete.text: Killing is a dirty business, but you did your job well, $N. If I weren't obligated to stay with the Prospector and Merrin, I'd be down there shedding blood right along side you.
294-complete.title: Ormer's Revenge

295-accept.name: Ormer Ironbraid
295-accept.text: Now it's time to really make those dreaded Raptors regret their blood-thirst. Just down below there are scores of Mottled Scytheclaws and Mottled Razormaws. Make those rotten creatures pay by slaying 10 of each!
295-accept.title: Ormer's Revenge

295-complete.name: Ormer Ironbraid
295-complete.text: You did a bang-up job of clearing out those raptors, $N!
295-complete.title: Ormer's Revenge

296-accept.name: Ormer Ironbraid
296-accept.text:
While you were down there I happened to notice that one of those beasts stood out from the rest. He was bigger and more menacing. I bet he's the one who led the others here to cause the disruption to the dig site.

I ask of you now one final task, $N. See to it that Sarltooth is brought to justice. And considering the gravity of his crimes, justice in this case means death! Bring me one of his talons as proof of his death.
296-accept.title: Ormer's Revenge

296-complete.name: Ormer Ironbraid
296-complete.text: Thank you, $N. Your efforts here will not be forgotten. Many innocent Dwarves died at this site, simply doing their jobs. The vengeance you delivered to those evil creatures should make them think twice before attacking King Magni's subjects ever again.
296-complete.title: Ormer's Revenge

296-progress.name: Ormer Ironbraid
296-progress.text: Is Sarltooth dead? Have you redeemed the memory of the fallen?
296-progress.title: Ormer's Revenge

299-complete.name: Prospector Whelgar
299-complete.text: Ah the Goaz Stone is complete! Fine work, $N. Fine work indeed. Now I can continue with the delicate translation of this Titan script. I can make out new words already! Hmm...it says here, "Old Gods... Chained Beneath the Land." This is the beginning of something epic.
299-complete.title: Uncovering the Past

299-progress.name: Prospector Whelgar
299-progress.text: Have you uncovered the four fragments yet, $N?  Ados, Modr, Golm and Neru...
299-progress.title: Uncovering the Past

323-accept.name: Sven Yorgen
323-accept.text:
Morbent Fel is a necromancer, and an ally to the dark riders.  I would pit you against the power of Morbent Fel, but I will not send you against that vile fiend without first knowing your strength.

You have already proven your bravery to me, but if you truly wish to face the necromancer, then you must now prove your skill against his minions.
323-accept.title: Proving Your Worth

337-accept.name: Unknown
337-accept.text:
Although the cover of this book is marred by scratches and caked with mud, the words "The History of Stormwind" can still be read along its spine.  Upon opening the book, the seal of the Stormwind Library is clearly stamped on the book's first page.

It looks like someone checked out this book, and never returned it...
337-accept.title: An Old History Book

337-complete.name: Milton Sheaf
337-complete.text:
Oh my!  This book hasn't rested on these shelves since before the rebuilding of Stormwind, years ago.  It will have to be restored of course, it's in bad shape, but I would be honored to place it within our rare books collection.

Thank you, madam.  Please accept this as payment for returning the book!
337-complete.title: An Old History Book

337-progress.name: Milton Sheaf
337-progress.text: Ooh!  What's that old book you have there?  Can I see it??
337-progress.title: An Old History Book

3765-complete.name: Gershala Nightwhisper
3765-complete.text: Ah, so my brother, Argos, sent you? I realize you must be weary from your travels. But we have much to talk about.
3765-complete.title: The Corruption Abroad

387-accept.name: Warden Thelwater
387-accept.text:
The uprising must be quelled!  I need your assistance.  If word gets out that the prison is overrun I will lose my job!  This is a case of foul play if I've ever seen one.  But what's important now is forcing these prisoners into submission for the safety of Stormwind.

The punishment for insurgency is death.  Kill some of these deviants!  That ought to get things under control.
387-accept.title: Quell the Uprising

388-accept.name: Nikova Raskol
388-accept.text:
Bitterness flows through my veins like a cold river.  My grandson, Mac, was such a good boy.  A mere 14 years old.  When the army was sent off to the front, Mac took up arms to defend the city.  He was a guard in The Stockade, where the Defias gang is locked up.  Mac reprimanded some of the prisoners for tearing their wool blankets to make scarves, a symbol of their gang.  For that Mac was stabbed in the back.

I want revenge.  Bring me 10 of their precious Wool Bandanas.  They are the color of blood.
388-accept.title: The Color of Blood

389-complete.name: Warden Thelwater
389-complete.text:
What in the Light do you want? Can't you see we have a crisis here?

Bazil Thredd?! Why would you want to speak with that bastard? How am I supposed to know you're not one of his cronies, come down to help with his bloody riot? If all the blasted cells weren't open, I might throw you in one for a while!
389-complete.title: Bazil Thredd

391-accept.name: Warden Thelwater
391-accept.text:
Let's get one thing straight, $N: I don't trust you. But, with the situation as it is, you probably won't make a difference.

So here's how it's going to be: go down there and have your talk with Thredd. If you're really on our side, then kill him and bring me his head when the job's done. And if it turns out you're on his side, and don't come out... when we find you, you'll die along with the rest of the maggots.
391-accept.title: The Stockade Riots

453-accept.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
453-accept.text:
Good luck, $N.  I hope you find the chap, and I hope you find him alive.

If he's left the safety of Darkshire then he could be prey to the beasts of the wilds.
453-accept.title: Finding the Shadowy Figure

453-complete.name: Jitters
453-complete.text:
<Jitters sighs...>

Yes, I'm the author of that book.  You finally found me, eh?

Well if you read that journal...then you only know the half of it!
453-complete.title: Finding the Shadowy Figure

453-progress.name: Jitters
453-progress.text: Who are you??  Leave me be!
453-progress.title: Finding the Shadowy Figure

471-complete.name: James Halloran
471-complete.text:
Hmm... Don't suppose you'd be interested in becoming my apprentice, would you?

Hah! No, I'm just kidding. You're much too old, for one thing. Besides - from the looks of you, it would seem that you have other ambitions in life. Nonetheless, these are some fine skins you've procured, and I'll be able to put them to good use.
471-complete.title: Apprentice's Duties

471-progress.name: James Halloran
471-progress.text:
My apprentice is like a son to me. It's going to be hard for him to live his life with only one leg.

Ah, $N, how goes it?  Do you have my skins?
471-progress.title: Apprentice's Duties

472-accept.name: Harlo Barnaby
472-accept.text:
Dun Modr has fallen to the Dark Iron Dwarves!

My wounds are grave, $c.  Most of the regiment was killed!  The Dark Iron thugs attacked us before we could regroup from the Thandol Span ambush.

Our leader, Longbraid, sounded the retreat horn.  As we left the town I was hit by a stray axe in the back.  All went black.

I awoke here in Menethil but I fear for my fellow soldiers.  Hope still burns within me.  Perhaps Longbraid is still alive!  See if you can find him near Dun Modr, $r!
472-accept.title: Fall of Dun Modr

538-accept.name: Milton Sheaf
538-accept.text:
$N.  If you don't mind a long journey then I have a task for you, to again help Stormwind fill its library.

The old kingdom of Alterac fell after the great war, and it had a large collection of books.  It's a tragedy that the city is ruined, but even more tragic is all of their knowledge lost!  We must recover what we can.

Southshore is the closest town to the Ruins of Alterac.  Go there and speak with Loremaster Dibbs.  He can direct you to the ruins, and to what books may be found there.
538-accept.title: Southshore

56-complete.name: Commander Althea Ebonlocke
56-complete.text: Splendid, $N.  For your service to the people of Darkshire you shall be rewarded.
56-complete.title: The Night Watch

57-accept.name: Commander Althea Ebonlocke
57-accept.text: $N, I'm getting reports of an undead infestation in the forest!  If you're up to the job, journey to the Raven Hill graveyard and slay 15 of those vile Skeletal Fiends and 15 Skeletal Horrors.  There are also reports of skeletons just south of Darkshire, in and around Tranquil Gardens Cemetery.  The undead must be driven from Duskwood!
57-accept.title: The Night Watch

57-complete.name: Commander Althea Ebonlocke
57-complete.text: The people of Darkshire thank you, $N.  You have proven yourself to be a great ally of The Night Watch.
57-complete.title: The Night Watch

58-accept.name: Commander Althea Ebonlocke
58-accept.text: The situation in Raven Hill is still grim.  The safety of Darkshire is in your hands, $N.  I don't have enough Watchers to keep the town safe.  We need you to dispatch for Raven Hill yet again and rid the eastern mausoleum of 20 Plague Spreaders!
58-accept.title: The Night Watch

66-accept.name: Madame Eva
66-accept.text:
Last night a horrible disturbance rippled through my veins.  I sensed that my granddaughter, Alyssa, was in great danger.  I consulted the cards and Death stared up at me from the table.

After taking a long journey through a dark trance I was able to uncover a clue to this terrifying mystery.  A name came to me, the name of Stalvan.

Seek out the Clerk in the Town Hall and see if you can find out more about this character.  I fear for us all.
66-accept.title: The Legend of Stalvan

66-complete.name: Clerk Daltry
66-complete.text: Ah so Madame Eva sent you. . . .
66-complete.title: The Legend of Stalvan

67-accept.name: Clerk Daltry
67-accept.text:
Stalvan, eh?  Let me check the town registry.

Stalvan. . .Stalvan. . .let's see.  Ah, here we go!  I have a record of a Mr. Stalvan Mistmantle.  The last recorded address is the Moonbrook Schoolhouse.  My, talk about outdated!

Do me a favor will you, friend?  If you happen to go out to Moonbrook, let me know if you get any update on this fellow.  I like to keep the records clean.
67-accept.title: The Legend of Stalvan

You place the Glyph of Azora on the stone.  It adheres itself ... and you hear from it Theocritus' disembodied voice:

You have my gratitude, young $N.  You may now speak with me through this Glyph, and I might have future tasks for you ... after I have probed the thoughts of my rival.

94-progress.text:
This Lion Statue has sat here for decades, and keeps a lonely watch over the infamous Tower of Ilgalar.

There is a depression at the base of the statue, where a gem or glyph might be set...
94-progress.title: A Watchful Eye
